one_liner: Senior federal buyer at CMS who writes solicitations, analyzes contractor prices, negotiates and administers health-program contracts under the FAR.
fit_summary: This GS-13 job requires 4 years of contracting experience, including a year doing cost/price analysis, negotiation strategy and preparing contract documents at a GS-12 level. It also requires a bachelor's degree with 24 business-related semester hours and agency-mandated contracting training (FAC-C/DAU-type). Daniel's known IEM consulting work on emergency management and policy knowledge don't show that background, so Daniel likely won't qualify unless the IEM role actually involved hands-on government contracting.
eligibility: Open to the public and to federal transition (fed-transition) applicants; no status or clearance required.
At least 52 weeks of specialized experience equivalent to GS-12 covering all three areas: cost and price analysis, negotiation strategies, and preparing all contract documents.
At least 4 years of experience in contracting or related positions, plus completion of agency-mandated training for GS-13 contracting levels.

Bachelor's degree with at least 24 semester hours in accounting, business, finance, law, contracts, purchasing, economics, industrial management, marketing, quantitative methods, or organization and management. Transcripts are required at application.
An online assessment with a cut score is required, in addition to the occupational questionnaire.
strategy: First, inventory your IEM work honestly. Did you price proposals, review cost breakdowns, negotiate with government contracting officers, or draft contract/proposal documents? If none of that applies, skip this GS-13 and target GS-1102 entry roles (GS-7/9) or acquisition intern programs instead.
Check your transcript before investing time. Count semester hours in business, economics, law, finance, management and related fields; you need 24.

If you do apply, describe the contracting-related IEM work in your own words, with dates and hours per week, mapped to each of the three specialized-experience items. Copying the announcement text gets you rated ineligible.
Fit everything on two pages: put the contracting-relevant role first, and compress unrelated work to one line each.
Answer the occupational questionnaire only at the level your resume supports. Overstating gets you removed, and an SME may review your resume.
The posting is open until 2027-01-15, but submit early, then complete the online assessment promptly and upload transcripts.
resume_bullets: Analyzed [number] cost proposals/cost breakdowns for [type of government client] contracts valued at [$ amount], assessing labor rates and other direct costs for reasonableness against [FAR/client requirements].
Developed negotiation positions and led discussions with [government client/subcontractors] on [scope/price/terms], resulting in [documented outcome].
Drafted [statements of work, solicitation sections, modifications, task orders] for [emergency management/disaster recovery] programs, ensuring compliance with [FAR clauses/client policies].
interview_questions: Walk us through how you perform a cost/price analysis and determine that a price is fair and reasonable.
Describe a negotiation you planned and led: what was your strategy, and what was the result?
How do you ensure a solicitation incorporates the required FAR and HHS provisions?
Tell us about managing a difficult contractor or stakeholder relationship during contract administration.
watch_outs: The 4-year contracting experience and mandatory GS-13 contracting training requirements will likely disqualify you without a real acquisition background.
Missing transcripts at application means an automatic ineligible rating.
The location is listed as Multiple Locations with no remote option. Confirm a Baltimore/Woodlawn-area or DC-area duty station is commutable from Manassas, even with telework.
